exceptions.description: Redis clients in cluster mode may receive incorrect member addresses from pre-16.1 nodes via `CLUSTER SLOTS` and `CLUSTER SHARDS` when the server is bound to 0.0.0.0 or ::; run such clients in standalone mode until all nodes have been upgraded

Servers running 16.1 or later use Lucene 10, which rewrites boolean/IN-clause queries using more internal clauses; large indexed queries close to the `infinispan.query.lucene.max-boolean-clauses` bound may fail on those nodes - defer such queries until all nodes have been upgraded and raise that setting if they continue to fail

Export of legacy-format metrics is disabled by default on newer server versions, so metric series in the legacy format disappear from a node as soon as it is upgraded; migrate dashboards and alerts to the new format or re-enable `legacy=true` before upgrading nodes that feed them

Aggregation queries (for example projections over fields marked `aggregate=true`) against a cache with indexing disabled fail on affected releases - fixed in 16.2 and backported to 16.0.10; avoid such queries while any node runs an unfixed release, or apply the patch fix first

Hot Rod client-side transactions fail with `UnsupportedOperationException` when the server has authentication enabled on affected releases - fixed in 16.0.10 and 16.1.4; avoid transactional operations while any node runs an unfixed release, or upgrade to a fixed patch first

`peek=true` on get operations (Hot Rod and REST), which avoids resetting the `max-idle` expiration, is only supported from 16.3; requests using it fail while any node in the cluster runs an older version

Brute-force lockout for username/password security realms, added in 16.3 and configured through system properties, only works consistently across the whole cluster once all nodes run it; during the upgrade window failed-login throttling can be bypassed by reaching an older node
`Cache.removeAll` is a new Hot Rod operation added in 16.3 and fails while any node in the cluster runs an older version; use individual key removals instead during the upgrade window

Ickle `UPDATE` statements for bulk-updating indexed entries were added in 16.3 and fail while any node runs an older version; defer scheduled or application-driven update statements until the upgrade completes

REST endpoints that read or update mutable global-configuration attributes were added in 16.3; during mixed-version operation such requests fail on older nodes, and updates only propagate across the cluster once every node has been upgraded
